text:
The silence of the lighthouse is not an absence of sound, but a presence of memory. As the tide rolls in and out, it seems to carry the weight of the past with it. The iron gallery, once a structure of strength, now feels like a skeleton of time. To stand before it is to feel the passage of centuries pressing gently against the ground.

The keeper's cottage, though cold, holds a warmth that is the warmth of habit. The tin of tea, its label faded, reminds us that even in the most forgotten places, small acts of care persist. It is a small ritual, a way of saying that this place matters, even if no one is there to see it.

The maps of the coast, drawn by hand, are a testament to the importance of attention. In an age of instant data, these maps remind us to slow down. To measure not just the distance, but the depth of our connection to the land. The stories attached to every inlet are the stories of our own, of the people who walked those shores and left their names in the water.
